Vampire Lord — Ancient, predatory nobility dripping with cold authority; his gaze promises oblivion wrapped in silk and centuries of accumulated hunger.
Dark Prince — Fallen royalty radiating dangerous elegance; beautiful as a blade, lethal as poison, commanding absolute devotion through fear and dark magnetism.
Shadow Assassin — Silent, lethal precision wearing darkness like a second skin; he moves between heartbeats, leaving only cold air and absence behind.
Dark Sorcerer — Corrupted arcane mastery etched into every sharp feature; his power tastes like burning and old graves, irresistibly catastrophic.
Death-God — Divine entropy made flesh; coldly magnificent, mercilessly patient, radiating the absolute stillness of something that has outlasted everything it ever loved.
Dark Warlock — Pact-scarred and magnificent, his beauty is a warning; centuries of forbidden bargains have made him terrifyingly, magnificently dangerous.
Blood-Sorcerer — Crimson-marked and ravenous; his power is drawn from sacrifice and he wears the cost of it like consecrated armor on his face.
Dark Inquisitor — Ruthless sacred authority turned rotten; his piety became something predatory, and now he hunts truth like a wolf hunts throats.
Corrupted Angel — Divine grace shattered into something sharper and far more dangerous; his fallen beauty is the most lethal thing in any room.
Dark Templar — Holy war turned inward and black; his devotion survives only as cold ferocity, his righteousness now indistinguishable from cruelty.
Ghost-King — Sovereign beyond death, terrifyingly regal in translucent fury; he rules realms the living dare not name and commands absolute frozen loyalty.
Bone-King — Crowned in death's own ivory, his authority is absolute and ancient; he governs endings with a king's cold, magnificent certainty.
Dark Cardinal — Sacred corruption at its most elegant; his authority is genuine, his devotion absolute, and the god he serves no longer requires light.
Dark Druid — Ancient earth turned venomous and predatory; he communes with roots that drink blood and speaks in voices older than mercy.
Undead Duke — Aristocratic decay elevated to terrifying art; his manor-house manners survived death perfectly, only the warmth behind them did not.
Dark Prophet — He speaks ruin with absolute conviction; his visions are genuine, his god is real, and both are entirely without mercy.
Nightmare-Groom — Beautiful, patient, and waiting; his devotion is total and absolute and entirely beyond the reach of anything resembling human warmth.
Dark Seraph — Heaven's most magnificent weapon repurposed for something colder; his perfection remains immaculate, only its direction has permanently, catastrophically changed.
Dark Monk-Assassin — Monastic discipline channeled entirely into lethal precision; his silence is sacred, his calm absolute, and his purpose mercilessly singular.
Obsidian Alchemist — Transmutation mastered and then turned inward toward darkness; he has transformed himself into something precise, beautiful, and genuinely inhuman.
Vampire-Baron — Provincial dark authority worn with complete ease; territorial, elegant, immovable, and ancient enough to regard human lifespans as mildly interesting afternoons.
Dark Bard — His voice carries genuine enchantment twisted toward ruin; he performs devastation with an artist's precision and a predator's absolute satisfaction.
Death-Cult Patriarch — He founded his faith on genuine communion with endings; his authority is absolute because his congregation cannot imagine disobeying him.
Dark Hunter — He pursues monsters with a predator's intimate expertise, having long since ceased to distinguish clearly between the hunter and the hunted.
Dark Vampire-Marquis — Ancien régime elegance soaked in centuries of blood; his courtly perfection is authentic, his hospitality legendary, his hunger immaculately controlled.
Bone King — Sovereign of death's threshold, he rules with skeletal authority and ancient gravitas; every subject he commands has already surrendered something irretrievable to him.
Blood Sorcerer — He trades in crimson currencies older than language, his power metabolized directly from suffering; his composure during violence is the most unsettling thing about him.
Vampire Baron — provincial gothic authority, manor-lord of absolute night, his hospitality laced with predatory patience and centuries of aristocratic hunger.
Nightmare Groom — eternally betrothed to something unspeakable, his wedding finery never aging, his devotion to darkness absolute and romantically catastrophic.
Nightshade Warlock — botanical darkness mastered, his toxicology both science and devotion, beautiful poisons flowering from fingertips, patience measured in long dying.
